algorithms.name: Sparse Contextual Bandits (FTRL with negative entropy + log-barrier over shrunk simplex, Algorithm 1)

symbols.s: sparsity level: ||l_t||_2^2 <= s for all t

conditions: losses are non-positive with ||l_t||_inf <= 1 (used in the stability lemma proof; reduction gives l_t in {-1,0}^K)

source.label: thm:upper-bound-sparse
source.quote: Let $\Pi \subseteq \brk[c]{\calX \to \calA}$ be a finite policy class of size $N$ where $\abs{\calA} = K$, and let $T \geq 1$. Then for any $s$-sparse contextual bandit instance over $\Pi$, the expected regret of \cref{alg:alg} with $\eta = \sqrt{{\log(N)}/{sT}}$, $\nu = {1}/{16}$ and $\eps = {1}/{NT}$ is at most $O \brk*{N \log \brk*{NT} + \sqrt{sT \log N}}$.

results.notes: N is the size of the policy class (N_exp). Proof gives explicit 16 N log(NT) + 2 sqrt(sT log N) (+2). Non-positivity of losses is required by the proof of Lemma 2 though not stated in the theorem. Regret defined via inf over policies of E[sum l_t(a_t)] - sum l_t(pi(x_t)); recorded as pseudo-regret.

conditions: finite hypothesis class of size N_exp

source.label: thm:upper-bound-main
source.quote: Let $\calH \subseteq \brk[c]{\calX \to \calY}$ be a finite hypothesis class with $\abs{\calH} = N$ and $\abs{\calY} = K \leq N$, and let $T \geq 1$. Then there exists an algorithm which, for any bandit multiclass classification instance over $\calH$, guarantees an expected regret bound of at most $O \brk*{\min \brk[c]*{\sqrt{KT \log N},~ N \log \brk*{NT} + \sqrt{T \log N}}}$.

results.notes: Statement is existential: achieved by running Algorithm 1 (s=1 via reduction) or EXP4, whichever bound is smaller. Comparator is best hypothesis in H. Regret defined with expectations (paper footnote: pseudo-regret).

source.label: thm:bandit_multiclass_lb
source.quote: For any (possibly randomized) bandit multiclass online algorithm and for all integers $K,N,T \geq 1$, there exists a stochastic bandit multiclass instance with $K+1$ labels over a hypothesis class $\calH$ of size $N $, where the algorithm must incur an expected regret of at least $\widetilde{\Omega} \brk!{ \min \brk[c]!{ N+\sqrt{T}, \sqrt{KT} } }$.

results.notes: Proof gives explicit 10^-4/sqrt(log K) * min{N, sqrt(KT)} in the case N >= sqrt(T), plus a 2-armed Omega(sqrt T) bound otherwise. Paper notes it also holds with deterministic labels.
